title: A Photonic-CXL Memory Appliance for Scalable KV Cache Management in LLM Inference
event_hint: Photonic-CXL switch-free shared-memory appliance for large-scale KV caches
problem: LLM KV caches require tens of terabytes at hundreds of GB/s, but GPU HBM, host DRAM, SSD, electrical CXL, and network transfer tiers each trade capacity, bandwidth, latency, or power. Disaggregated prefill/decode further makes KV movement a TTFT bottleneck and cache eviction causes latency cliffs.
mechanism: The Marvell Photonic Fabric Memory Appliance replaces electrical CXL switches with a passive optical-fiber shuffle and switch-free full crossbar, providing shared memory across hosts. The photonic-CXL design targets 32 TB pooled capacity, 128 GB/s unidirectional bandwidth per host, and up to 16 hosts; it is integrated with vLLM/LMCache-style tiers to retrieve KV blocks from pooled memory and avoid eviction-driven recomputation.

evidence.claim: Host-memory KV retrieval reaches up to 100x speedup over GPU recomputation, while SSD retrieval reaches at most 9.7x in the tested configurations.
evidence.value: up to 100x host; up to 9.7x SSD
evidence.source_locator: PDF pages 2-3, Characterization and Table I

evidence.claim: The PF Memory Appliance provides 32 TB shared memory across up to 16 hosts with 128 GB/s unidirectional bandwidth per host.
Hardware emulation shows over 50% latency reduction versus electrical CXL switched memory pools.
End-to-end serving simulation improves TTFT by 6.6x for multi-turn conversations and sustains flat TTFT as workload scales to 300 concurrent conversations.
evidence.condition: Photonic Fabric Memory Appliance augmented serving simulation

evidence.claim: The repeated-request characterization covers A100, H100, and H200 systems, LLaMA models from 8B to 405B, and contexts up to 4M tokens.
evidence.condition: 100% cache-hit repeated-request benchmark with vLLM and LMCache

evaluation_context: The paper combines repeated-request characterization on local/cloud A100/H100/H200 systems, emulation of the photonic-CXL appliance, and end-to-end serving simulations. The characterization uses vLLM with LMCache, batch sizes 1/2/8/16/32, contexts up to 4M tokens, and 100% cache-hit conditions; appliance results are emulated/simulated rather than a deployed hardware measurement.
limitations: The 32 TB/128 GB/s appliance and >50% latency reduction are architecture/emulation results, not production deployment evidence. End-to-end 6.6x TTFT is a simulation under specified multi-turn and eviction conditions; network contention, optical fault behavior, CXL coherence overhead, software integration cost, and real workload hit rates are not established. Host-memory speedups depend strongly on model size, context length, batch, PCIe bandwidth, and the no-cache recomputation baseline; SSD can be slower than recomputation in some cases (inference).
project_relevance: This is a hardware substrate for treating KV cache as a pooled, network-adjacent memory resource: it targets capacity-bandwidth gaps before TPN policy decides placement or transfer. For project evaluation, separate cache eviction rate, pooled-memory latency/bandwidth, TTFT tail, concurrent users, and photonic/CXL failure recovery; do not conflate emulated appliance gains with scheduler gains (inference).
